records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
search_queries: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
records.answer:
Master's students on a J-1 can do Academic Training (AT) for up to **18 months, or the length of their degree program, whichever is shorter**. Students pursuing a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension. [(ISSS Academic Training page)](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/j1-employment)

Key conditions:
- AT during your studies and AT after your program ends are added together toward the limit. Full-time and part-time AT count equally.
- AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date, and it must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.
- It must be directly related to your major field of study on your DS-2019.
- Submit your request to ISSS at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends allowing about three weeks for processing. The form is on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx).

On the duration of status rule: DHS published a final rule on July 17, 2026 that would require USCIS extensions for post-completion AT. However, a federal court [postponed its effective date on September 14, 2026](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status) and barred DHS from implementing it. ISSS is monitoring the situation.

For details on the STEM extension or your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

grade.explanation: The 18-month (or program length, whichever is shorter) limit for master's students is correct and supported. However, the answer says the July 2026 final rule would require USCIS extensions for post-completion AT, but that excerpt mentions only extra program time and post-completion OPT; AT appears only in the 2025 proposed rule.
